set.body:
Journey 1 of docs/plan.md.

Done when
A study held in the legacy XNAT is pulled, converted to BIDS with standard tools and a per-study mapping, reviewed in the browser and accepted. Its XNAT origin is recorded. IN6 is the acceptance rehearsal.

Design decisions
- XNAT stays the scanner-facing DICOM archive. Sanctity pulls from it and never writes to it.
- Conversion runs out of process: a pinned dcm2niix plus a declarative per-study mapping. Sanctity does not reimplement DICOM-to-BIDS heuristics that dcm2bids and heudiconv already provide.
- The tool lives in tools/xnat2bids (Python) and hands its output to Sanctity through the operator import command (IN4).
- The in-process adapters in modules/import-xnat and modules/import-dicom stay as they are. Today they verify one XNAT file collection at a time and map T1w, T2w, bold and sbref only, and nothing in the service calls them. Extending them is parked under C01.
- Original DICOM stays in XNAT for now. The release records the source system, counts and digests. The table that links XNAT labels to BIDS labels is a re-identification key: it stays with the study's custodian, outside the release and outside the repository.
- EEG, MEG and eye-tracking data do not live in XNAT. They arrive already in BIDS, or as an archive deposit. A conversion kit for them is later work.

Order
IN1 (owner) runs alongside IN2, IN3 and IN4. IN5 is independent. IN6 closes the journey.
set.title: IN: Bring a study in from the legacy XNAT as BIDS
